docs.contenu:
🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
- Recognise cause-and-consequence relationships in a sentence.
- Use a wide range of linkers to express cause (because, since, as, due to) and consequence (so, therefore, as a result, consequently).
- Choose the correct grammar after each linker (clause or noun phrase).
- Combine short sentences into longer, well-connected ones for clearer writing.

🔍 Warm-up
Read: "The roads were icy. Many buses were late." These two facts are clearly linked, but nothing joins them. Now add a linker: "Because the roads were icy, many buses were late." The sentence is instantly clearer. Cause-and-consequence linkers show WHY something happens and WHAT results from it.

I. LINKERS OF CAUSE
📘 Rules and definitions
A cause is the reason something happens. The most common cause linkers are: because, since, as, seeing that, due to, owing to, because of.
- because / since / as / seeing that are followed by a full clause (subject + verb): "because it rained".
- due to / owing to / because of are followed by a noun or noun phrase: "because of the rain".

📝 Grammar patterns and usage
Study the difference carefully:
- Clause: "The match was cancelled because the pitch was flooded."
- Noun phrase: "The match was cancelled because of the flooded pitch."
"Since" and "as" often begin the sentence: "As the shops were closed, we went home." "Since" can also mean "from a time", so read the context.

✏️ Worked examples
- "Since prices have risen, families are spending less." (cause = prices have risen)
- "The flight was delayed owing to heavy fog." (cause = heavy fog, a noun phrase)
- "As she was tired, she went to bed early." (cause = she was tired)
Each sentence answers the question "Why?"

II. LINKERS OF CONSEQUENCE
📘 Rules and definitions
A consequence (or result) is what happens because of a cause. Common consequence linkers are: so, therefore, thus, as a result, consequently, for this reason, that is why.
- so joins two clauses in one sentence: "It was late, so we left."
- therefore, consequently, as a result usually start a new sentence or follow a semicolon and are set off by a comma.

📝 Grammar patterns and usage
Punctuation matters:
- "The bridge was closed; therefore, drivers used another route."
- "The bridge was closed. As a result, drivers used another route."
- "The bridge was closed, so drivers used another route."
Notice that "so" is informal-neutral, while "therefore" and "consequently" are more formal and suit essays.

✏️ Worked examples
- "The team trained hard; therefore, they won the final." (result = they won)
- "Fuel became expensive, so more people cycled to work." (result = more cycling)
- "The report was late. Consequently, the meeting was postponed." (result = postponed meeting)

III. COMBINING AND VARYING SENTENCES
📘 Rules and definitions
Cause and consequence are two sides of the same relationship. The same idea can be written from either side:
- Cause first: "Because the alarm failed, the workers were not warned."
- Consequence first: "The workers were not warned; the alarm had failed."
Good writers vary their linkers so that a paragraph never repeats the same word.

🛠️ Writing method
To join two short sentences:
1. Decide which fact is the cause and which is the result.
2. Choose a cause linker (because, since, due to) OR a consequence linker (so, therefore).
3. Check the grammar: clause or noun phrase after the linker.
4. Add correct punctuation.
5. Reread to be sure the meaning did not change.

✏️ Worked examples
Start: "It was raining. The match was postponed."
- With cause: "The match was postponed because it was raining."
- With consequence: "It was raining, so the match was postponed."
- Formal version: "It was raining; therefore, the match was postponed."

👀 Notes
Do not use two linkers for the same relationship in one sentence. "Because it was late, so we left" is wrong: choose ONE, either "Because it was late, we left" or "It was late, so we left." One relationship needs only one linker.

⚠️ Common mistakes
- Writing "because of" before a full clause: WRONG "because of it rained". Use "because it rained" or "because of the rain".
- Doubling linkers: "Because... so...".
- Forgetting the comma after "Therefore," or "As a result," at the start of a sentence.
- Confusing "since" (cause) with "since" (time) without checking the context.
- Overusing "so" in formal writing instead of "therefore" or "as a result".

⭐ To remember
- Cause answers "Why?"; consequence answers "What happened next?".
- Clause linkers: because, since, as. Noun-phrase linkers: due to, owing to, because of.
- Consequence linkers: so, therefore, as a result, consequently.
- Use only one linker per relationship, with correct punctuation.

🔗 Applications
These linkers are essential in argumentative and for-and-against essays, where you must explain why an argument matters and what result it leads to. They also make reports, letters and spoken explanations far clearer and more convincing.

enonce.question:
Complete the sentences with the appropriate cause or consequence linker from the list: because, so, since, therefore, as.
1. She missed the bus _____ she woke up late.
2. The weather was bad; _____, we stayed at home.
3. _____ he studied hard, he passed the exam.
4. _____ it was raining, we took an umbrella.
5. He didn’t eat breakfast; _____, he felt hungry all morning.
Choose the correct word: 'The concert was cancelled ______ the storm.' (because / because of)
Label each linker as CAUSE or CONSEQUENCE: since, therefore, due to, as a result.
Fill the gap with 'so': 'The library was closed, ______ we studied at home.'

Rewrite the following sentences using the linker in brackets. Make any necessary changes.
1. He didn’t go to school. He was sick. (because of)
2. The traffic was heavy. We arrived late. (as a result)
3. She didn’t study. She failed the test. (so)
4. The movie was boring. We left early. (therefore)
5. He was tired. He went to bed early. (since)
Correct the mistake: 'Because the road was blocked, so we took another way.'
Rewrite this sentence with 'therefore', using correct punctuation: 'The battery was flat, so the phone would not switch on.'
Join these two sentences using 'because': 'The exam was difficult. Many students failed it.'
Rewrite using 'due to' + noun phrase: 'The trains were delayed because it snowed heavily.'
Choose the correct linker: 'She studied every evening; ______, she passed with distinction.' (owing to / consequently)

Read the text and fill in the gaps with the appropriate cause or consequence linker from the list: because, so, since, therefore, as a result, consequently, for this reason.
Last weekend, I decided to go hiking in the mountains. _____ the weather was beautiful, I expected a great day out. However, I forgot to bring enough water. _____, I got dehydrated and had to cut my hike short. _____, my friends and I decided to go to a café instead. _____ I hadn’t prepared properly, I wasn’t dressed appropriately for the hike. _____, I caught a cold the next day. I won’t make the same mistake again!
Write a short paragraph (4-5 sentences) about pollution in cities. Use at least THREE different cause-and-consequence linkers and underline them.
Combine each pair into one sentence, using a DIFFERENT linker for each: (1) The alarm did not ring. She woke up late. (2) Prices increased. Sales dropped. (3) He trained daily. He improved quickly.

Read and correct all the linker errors in this paragraph: 'Because of the weather was bad, the trip was cancelled. The students were disappointed, therefore they organised an indoor activity instead. Since of the heavy rain, they stayed in the hall.'
